chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Sabbah al-Haddad, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) say: Visit al-Husayn (peace be upon him), even if it is only once a year. Indeed, whoever goes to him, knowing his right and not denying it, will have no recompense but Paradise. They will be granted abundant sustenance, and Allah will bring them immediate relief. Indeed, Allah has assigned four thousand angels to the grave of al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him); all of them weep for him and escort those who visit him to their families. If they become ill, the angels visit them, and if they die, the angels attend their funeral, seeking forgiveness for them and asking Allah to have mercy on them.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards and angelic duties associated with visiting Imam al-Husayn's grave?
ai.summary: Compiled by Ibn Qulawayh in *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, this hadith establishes Ziyarat al-Husayn as a means of securing divine reward, promising Paradise and abundant sustenance to those who visit with correct theological recognition (Ma'rifah). It highlights the cosmic significance of the event by describing four thousand angels weeping for Imam al-Husayn and actively attending to the visitors, thereby linking the physical act of pilgrimage with spiritual sustenance and divine mercy.
